2609.16627.title: Quantifying Organizational Environmental Action from Web Data and Large Language Models
2609.16627.paper_summary: Quantifying organizational environmental action from publicly available web content remains a challenging environmental data science problem because relevant information can be dispersed across multiple webpages and is primarily communicated through unstructured text. We present a scalable computational framework for transforming organizational web content into structured measures of environmental action and demonstrate the approach using Jewish congregations in the United States. We constructed a national database of 4,964 congregations by integrating multiple geospatial, knowledge-base, directory, and manually reviewed sources. Of these, 2,657 had active websites that were successfully crawled, producing a corpus of 154,454 webpages. We compared three approaches for detecting environmental actions: keyword retrieval followed by large language model (LLM) classification, semantic vector retrieval followed by LLM classification, and direct LLM classification classification without preliminary retrieval. Agreement with an expert human reviewer was lowest for keyword retrieval ($κ$ = 0.26), higher for semantic vector retrieval ($κ$ = 0.42), and similar for direct LLM classification ($κ$ = 0.40). Although semantic retrieval achieved the highest agreement, its retrieval recall was 0.87, indicating loss of relevant content before classification. Applied to the complete corpus, direct LLM classification identified at least one environmental action at 1,398 congregations (53%), providing greater coverage than either retrieval-based approach. These results demonstrate that preliminary retrieval can reduce computational cost but may exclude relevant information before it reaches the classifier. The framework provides a reproducible approach for extracting organization-level environmental information from unstructured web content that can be adapted to other institutions.
2609.16627.paper_summary_zh: 量化組織環境行動從公開可用的網頁內容中仍然是一個具有挑戰性的環境數據科學問題，因為相關信息可能分散在多個網頁上，並主要通過非結構化文本進行傳達。我們提出了一個可擴展的計算框架，用於將組織網頁內容轉換為結構化的環境行動指標，並使用美國的猶太會堂來演示這一方法。我們通過整合多個地理空間、知識庫、目錄和手動審查的來源，構建了一個包含4,964個會堂的全國數據庫。在這些會堂中，有2,657個擁有活躍的網站，成功被爬取，產生了154,454個網頁的語料庫。我們比較了三種檢測環境行動的方法：關鍵字檢索後接大型語言模型（LLM）分類、語義向量檢索後接LLM分類，以及不進行初步檢索的直接LLM分類。與專家人類審核者的一致性在關鍵字檢索中最低（$κ$ = 0.26），在語義向量檢索中較高（$κ$ = 0.42），而直接LLM分類則相似（$κ$ = 0.40）。儘管語義檢索達到了最高的一致性，其檢索召回率為0.87，顯示在分類之前損失了相關內容。應用於完整語料庫，直接LLM分類在1,398個會堂（53%）中識別出至少一項環境行動，提供了比任何基於檢索的方法更大的覆蓋範圍。這些結果表明，初步檢索可以降低計算成本，但可能在信息到達分類器之前排除相關信息。該框架提供了一種可重複的方法，用於從非結構化網頁內容中提取組織層級的環境信息，並可適用於其他機構。
